result.note: Tested the RBI's regulatory measures to curb rupee speculation and their stated effect on the rupee. Hedging-cost movements were skipped as market data.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank of India's measures to curb rupee speculation, as reported in April 2026:
items: The RBI capped banks' net open positions in foreign exchange at USD 100 million.
The RBI barred companies from rebooking forward contracts they had cancelled.
Following the measures, the rupee weakened by about 2% against the dollar.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the rupee rallied 2% toward the 93 level after the measures. The RBI also banned non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), which reduced market liquidity and pushed one-year dollar hedging costs up by the most since the 2008 financial crisis.
questions.source: To rein in the rupee, the central bank capped banks' net open positions at USD 100 million and banned companies from rebooking cancelled forward contracts, which we covered here and here.
